environment.description: Same Lambda function deployed on a custom container image (ECR) with the following runtime characteristics: Container image built with all layers flattened and rootfs mounted read-only by the Lambda container runtime (OCI spec 'rootfs.readonly=true' in image config). The /tmp mount point is NOT provisioned as a separate tmpfs volume — instead, the ephemeral storage configuration is set to 512MB but the mount namespace inherits the read-only propagation from the container rootfs overlay (this is achieved by setting the Lambda function's ephemeral storage path to a subdirectory within the read-only rootfs rather than a separate mount). Additionally, the container ENTRYPOINT uses a minimal init that sets process umask to 0777 and the Lambda extension layer intercepts all write(2)/open(2,O_WRONLY) syscalls via a seccomp-bpf profile loaded at container init (profile: deny-write-class, covering write, pwrite64, writev, openat with O_WRONLY|O_RDWR|O_CREAT|O_TRUNC flags). Network egress is restricted by a VPC security group with no outbound rules (0 egress rules, default deny-all outbound). The function's IAM execution role has an explicit Deny on all actions except logs:PutLogEvents via a permission boundary (arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNT:policy/lambda-readonly-boundary).

config.permission_boundary_effect: explicit Deny on all actions except logs:PutLogEvents
config.ephemeral_storage_note: path mapped within ro rootfs, not separate tmpfs
